text:
ashley: quick heads-up — for the EU tenant incident we want an SDK/API header pattern to force routing behavior for rollout testing and richer telemetry. can we agree a small set of headers?

kevin: what exactly do you want the SDK to send?

ashley: proposal: X-Redwood-Region-Hint: eu-west-1 (advisory), X-Redwood-Tier-Override: dedicated|standard|free, and routing.debug=true to emit full decision trace for that request. example:

ashley: ```
GET /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer <key>
X-Redwood-Region-Hint: eu-west-1
X-Redwood-Tier-Override: standard
X-Redwood-Debug: routing,trace
```

raj: we already accept a region hint but it's advisory only. for canaries we should support a `hint_mode` semantics: prefer | require. otherwise tests are flaky when capacity rebalance occurs.

maria: console UX notes: add per-rollout toggle "Honor SDK hints (prefer/require)" and surface a small badge when a request used SDK hints. also show fallback counts by region/model variant in the rollout detail panel.

kevin: telemetry changes: emit routing metrics with tags. suggested metric names: routing.hint_match (count), routing.fallback (count), routing.fallback_reason (count), routing.fallback_model_variant (count), routing.quota_block (count). attach tags: customer_id, region_hint, chosen_region, tier_override, model_variant, rollout_id, hint_mode.

ashley: we should also limit volume — add a per-request sample header e.g., X-Redwood-Debug-Sample: 1 to force 100% tracing for that request. SDK debug flags can set sampling to 100% only in dev.

raj: quota interplay question: if a tenant is near committed quota, do we let tier override bypass quota enforcement? i think no — overrides should not bypass tenant quotas unless an admin-level header X-Redwood-Bypass-Quota: true is present and validated. otherwise prefer lower-cost model variant or degrade gracefully.

maria: console graphs: in rollout UI we want a three-line chart: % served in requested region, fallback rate, and avg latency. add an alert rule if fallback spikes > 5% in 5m for a rollout. also add a "simulate" button that uses the SDK headers to run 10 sampled requests through the staging router and shows where they'd land.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/route-debug-headers -> staging (build 2025-11-05T12:10Z) :rocket:

kevin: implementation idea: add a debug simulation endpoint in the API: POST /v1/debug/simulate-routing with payload { "customer_id":"", "region_hint":"", "tier_override":"", "hint_mode":"prefer|require", "model_preferences": ["optim-quant","latency-opt"] } and return a deterministic predicted routing trace plus a sampled decision log. helpful for support & console.

ashley: agree. ensure the simulate endpoint respects auth + RBAC and marks traces with simulate=true so they don't count against real metrics. TTL traces to 24h.

raj: i'll draft a runtime PR: add hint_mode support, honor require in canary routes only, add trace storage (kv namespace) keyed by trace_id, and emit the metric tags Kevin listed. will include a simple tracing proto for the decision path. assigning to @raj.

maria: i'll duo with @ashley on console mockups and open the ticket linking to the simulate endpoint doc + mock telemetry queries.

ashley: thanks all. one more small request: add a short log line format for quick filtering in kibana: "routing.trace_id=%s customer=%s hint=eu-west chosen_region=us-east fallback=quantized-v2 reason=capacity tier_override=standard" — makes support reproduction easier. :thumbsup:

kevin: also add a low-verbosity enum for logs to avoid PII leakage (use customer_id tokenized).

raj: noted. i'll include tokenization and retention limits in the PR.

maria: looks good. i'll track console work in the rollout epic and link the staging deploy when it's up. :eyes:
